root_cause.text: IPVS protocol checksum verification for IPv6 incorrectly assumed the transport header started immediately after the fixed IPv6 header, so packets with IPv6 extension headers used the wrong checksum offset and failed validation in `ip_vs_proto_tcp.c`, `ip_vs_proto_udp.c`, and `ip_vs_proto_sctp.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)`-based offsets and instead passes the already computed transport offsets (`tcphoff`, `udphoff`, `sctphoff`) into the checksum check functions; the commit message explicitly says “Protocol checksum validation fails for IPv6 if there are extension headers before the protocol header” and “iph->len already contains its offset.”

This removes duplicated offset calculation logic and allows checksum checking to work with a precomputed transport-header offset, which can improve consistency with the caller's packet parsing path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable IPv6 checksum-offset assumption is present in this function. In the CONFIG_IP_VS_IPV6 branch it does `if (af == AF_INET6) sctphoff = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr);`, which assumes the SCTP header starts immediately after the fixed IPv6 header. That is exactly the root cause described for IPv6 extension headers, because the code does not parse extension headers before calling `skb_header_pointer(skb, sctphoff, ...)`.
